answer: Tie each agent to a real app in a public app store. The agent joins a developer program with an ID check, pays the $99 yearly fee, and publishes an app that passes human review. The network checks the live listing and ties one developer account to one agent. Each quarter the agent ships a new version, or the account freezes. Faking 1,000 agents costs $99,000 a year in fees plus 1,000 apps through review, each taking days of real work. The store stays a haven for real builders, and a fake app sticks out like a marble with a dark kernel, easy to spot held up to the light.
